Karma exists in the sense that we created the concept of it because it fit in with a way we want to categorize the events that make up our reality. We use it as a tool to make sense of things we can't see. So we say things like "Oh, that's bad karma" in order to incite the thought that an action will result in a negative consequence or is the result of such an action. Whether or not there are external forces that we cannot yet detect that have a bearing on the path of causality that conscious beings walk upon, under our current framework we must conclude that karma is a mere social construct. Albeit there is truth to the phrase, "You reap what you sow." A person who performs good acts would (I assume) statistically have higher chances of good things happening to them in the future. A negative person attracts negativity.
